knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Keeping both feet on the ground and moving along the stair removes the fall risk that leaning or standing on a tread creates.
Equipment kept to one side of the landing does not obstruct people and cannot be knocked off a tread.
A wet tread is a fall hazard. The spill is wiped at once and the tread dried before the worker leaves it.

practicalCriteria: Places warning signs on each landing before work starts, observed by the assessor.
Cleans a handrail section with both feet on the ground and without leaning or standing on a tread, observed by the assessor.
Clears a simulated spill and dries the tread before the warning sign is removed, observed by the assessor.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80 per cent pass mark, so all three must be correct. Practical competence: assessor sign-off against each practical criterion, observed on site or in a simulated stairwell. A knowledge-check pass does not verify practical competence. Height work is outside this assessment and is referred to the supervisor.
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation sheet for the stairwell task
Stair and landing checklist showing signs, drying check and any referred section
stopWorkCriteria: The worker stands on a tread or leans over the rail to reach a section
A bucket or vacuum is left on a step
Work at height is attempted without the supervisor's direction and the business's height-work procedure
